newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds spring back, outperform U.S.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds spring back, outperform U.S.

text.p: Australian bonds put in a more positive performance after the sharp downward correction of the last two days to outperform a rebound in the U.S. bond market.
Traders said the shake-out after the recent steep rally to near 2-1/2 year yield lows appears to have run its course and was luring in offshore bargain hunters today, traders said.
"The 35 basis points sell-down since Friday has provided some excellent buying opportunities and let's face it the fundamentals haven't changed in that time," one trader said.
The market was already on the bounce when Japan released its quarterly Tankan survey showing gloomy business conditions.

The local dollar rallied on the news as Japanese interest rates are now expected to be kept at current low levels, and this should keep Japanese investor demand for higher yielding Australian debt on the boil, both directly and through dual currency samuari issues.
U.S. Treasuries also rallied on Japan's poor outlook in Tokyo, extending Tuesday's technical gains seen in New York.

However, the local market outpaced the rally to claw back some of the corrective spread widening seen in the past few sessions. The 10-year spread to the U.S. narrowed to around 134 basis points from 142, but remains above Monday's early 120 low.

The local market also outpaced Canadian debt, which had a minor set-back from its recent sizeable outperformance after Ontario Hydro issued a C$500 million bond. Meanwhile, domestic bonds face July balance of payments on Thursday.
The 10-year bond contract ended the session testing 91.920 after faltering at the 91.940 to 91.985 congestion area.
